land.text: Masinissa's Numidia: 'He succeeded in defeating Syphax and unified Numidia (c. 203-202 BC)'; 'his kingdom was assimilated into the kingdom of Masinissa'

successors.note: The infobox says 'Annexed by Numidia: 175 BC' and lists Numidia (Roman province) and Mauretania as successors. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Numidia row starts in 197 BC.

capitals.name: Siga
capitals.note: The infobox lists 'Siga Cirta'; the body names Siga as the place 'whose first sovereign was Syphax' and the Syphax page has Syphax receive Scipio and Hasdrubal Gisco at Siga in 206 BC. The page gives no coordinates; the dot is placed at Tlemcen, the gazetteer's nearest town (Siga is near the Tafna mouth, some 40 km away). [Reviewer af-02-x: moved from Tlemcen to the Siga site in the lower Tafna valley, 35.2663 N 1.4499 W on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siga.]

capitals.name: Cirta (Constantine)
capitals.note: The Syphax page never names a capital but has Laelius and Masinissa pursue him to Cirta in 203 BC and his troops retreat 'to the capital city which later fell'; the infobox lists Cirta beside Siga. The year of the move is the researcher's, tied to the 206 BC conquest of the east.

correction.text: Western Numidia from the Mulucha (Moulouya) eastwards, the Oranais being the researcher's reading of the Siga country

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The kingdom of Massaesylia extended all the way west to Mulucha river'; the page gives no eastern limit and no date for any extent (the infobox: 'Established: 4th century BC'; the map caption 220 BC under Syphax). Strabo, as the page quotes him, has it begin 'at the river Molochath and end at Cape Tritonis' (not placed).

correction.text: the Tell from the Moulouya to Constantine, after Syphax 'conquered considerable parts of the eastern Numidian kingdom' in 206 BC

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'He ruled from present-day Constantine to the Moulouya' (no year); 'When Gala died in 206 BC... Syphax then conquered considerable parts of the eastern Numidian kingdom'. The northern Algerian provinces from Chlef to Skikda are the researcher's reading of that span and overstate a kingdom of cities and tribes.

region.text: Western Numidia between the Moulouya and the Oranais

ledger.note: c. 344 BC (page silent): the kingdom exists from the 4th century BC. The infobox gives 'Established: 4th century BC' and a ruler list opening '344-310 BC: Aylimas (?)'; the page names no founding event, year or extent beyond the Mulucha in the west.

region.text: the Tell from Chlef to Constantine

ledger.note: 206 BC: Syphax takes the east of the Massylii kingdom. 'When Gala died in 206 BC, his sons Masinissa and Oezalces quarreled about the inheritance'; Syphax 'conquered considerable parts of the eastern Numidian kingdom'; the Masaesyli page: after Gaia's death (c. 206 BC) 'Syphax attempted to seize his territories'. The page names no place; the Constantine end is from 'He ruled from present-day Constantine to the Moulouya'.
206 BC (bridge): the seat goes east to Cirta. The infobox lists 'Siga Cirta'; the Syphax page has him pursued to Cirta in 203 BC and has no year for the move.

region.text: the east of the kingdom, from Chlef to Constantine

ledger.note: 203 BC: Masinissa takes the east. 'In the 203 BC Battle of the Great Plains, Scipio overcame Gisco and Syphax', then Laelius and Masinissa pursued Syphax to Cirta; the capital 'later fell' (no year) as Masinissa claimed the kingdom.

c. 203-202 BC: Masinissa unifies Numidia. 'He succeeded in defeating Syphax and unified Numidia (c. 203-202 BC)'; Syphax 'died in Tibur in 203 or 202 BC' (infobox 202); the Masaesyli infobox annexes the kingdom to Numidia only in 175 BC.

wars.name: Syphax against the Massylii
wars.outcome: Syphax attacked the Massylii (undated, after his Roman alliance of 213 BC) and after Gala's death in 206 BC conquered considerable parts of the eastern kingdom; Masinissa and Oezalces quarrelled over the inheritance.
wars.note: The page dates the 213 BC alliance with Rome and Quintus Statorius's training of his troops, not the attack.

wars.name: Second Punic War in Africa
wars.outcome: Syphax met Scipio and Hasdrubal Gisco at Siga in 206 BC and later allied with Carthage (Gisco's daughter Sophonisba, no year); at the Battle of the Great Plains in 203 BC 'Scipio overcame Gisco and Syphax'; Laelius and Masinissa pursued him to Cirta and he was taken.
wars.note: The page gives no year for the capture; 203 BC is the Great Plains battle, the infobox has 'Battle of Cirta (POW)'.

certainty.note: The pages give one river in the west and 'Constantine' in the east, with no dated frontier; the Oranais and the Tell provinces are the researcher's.

notes: Cliopatria has no Masaesyli row (its Kingdom of Numidia row starts in 197 BC). The page has no rulers' reign years beyond '344-310 BC: Aylimas (?)' and '? -175 BC: Archobarzane'; Syphax's own reign is 'c. 225 - c. 203 BC' on his page (infobox) and the only date on the Masaesyli page is the 220 BC map caption; the dossier starts in 344 BC only to have a number (page silent, confidence 1). The end is the Masaesyli page's 'c. 203-202 BC' for Masinissa's unification; the infobox 'Annexed by Numidia: 175 BC' and the Syphax page's 'died in Tibur in 203 or 202 BC' are the other dates. The Syphax page says he was born at Siga c. 250 BC, allied with Rome in 213 BC, and concluded a treaty with Scipio only at Siga in 206 BC; the 'Massylii' kingdom of Gala has no dossier here (the Cliopatria row for Numidia begins in 197 BC). Cape Tritonis, Strabo's eastern limit as the page quotes him, is not in the gazetteer and is not placed.
